subject: chemistry
introduction: Quick-reference data for CSEC Chemistry: key equations, the reactivity series, periodic trends, and qualitative tests.

items.name: Avogadro's number
items.formula: 1 mole = 6.02 × 10²³ particles
items.notes: Particles = atoms, molecules, ions or electrons.

items.name: Moles from mass
items.formula: n = m / Mr  (mol)
items.notes: Mr = relative molecular/formula mass. Example: 40 g NaOH (Mr 40) = 1 mol.

items.name: Concentration
items.formula: c = n / V  (mol/dm³)
items.notes: V must be in dm³ (1000 cm³ = 1 dm³).

items.name: Molar gas volume (r.t.p.)
items.formula: 1 mol of any gas = 24 dm³ (24000 cm³)
items.notes: r.t.p. = room temperature and pressure. Example: 0.5 mol CO₂ = 12 dm³.

items.name: Empirical formula
items.formula: divide each % or mass by Ar, then simplest whole-number ratio
items.notes: Molecular formula = (empirical formula) × n.

items.name: Percentage yield / purity
items.formula: % = (actual / theoretical) × 100%
items.notes: Same form for percentage purity of a sample.

items.name: pH scale
items.formula: 0–6 acidic, 7 neutral, 8–14 alkaline
items.notes: Each pH unit = 10× change in H⁺ concentration. pH 2 is strongly acidic.

items.name: Neutralization (general)
items.formula: acid + base → salt + water
items.notes: Example: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.

items.name: Acid + metal
items.formula: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen
items.notes: Test for H₂: squeaky pop with a lighted splint.

items.name: Acid + carbonate
items.formula: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide
items.notes: Test for CO₂: turns limewater milky.

items.name: Ionic equation (neutralization)
items.formula: H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l)
items.notes: Spectator ions cancel out.

items.name: Titration reading
items.formula: titre = final burette reading − initial reading
items.notes: Average concordant titres (within 0.10 cm³) for the calculation.

items.name: OILRIG
items.formula: Oxidation Is Loss (of electrons); Reduction Is Gain
items.notes: Oxidation number rises = oxidized; falls = reduced.

items.name: Displacement example
items.formula: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
items.notes: Zinc is oxidized (0 → +2); copper ions reduced (+2 → 0).

items.name: Reactivity series (key order)
items.formula: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > (C) > Zn > Fe > (H) > Cu > Ag > Au
items.notes: Metals above carbon extracted by electrolysis; below by reduction with carbon/coke.

items.name: Electrolysis products (rules)
items.formula: cathode (−): metal or H₂ discharged; anode (+): non-metal or O₂ discharged
items.notes: Brine: H₂ at cathode, Cl₂ at anode. Molten PbBr₂: Pb at cathode, Br₂ at anode.

items.name: Rust prevention
items.formula: rusting needs oxygen AND water
items.notes: Prevent by painting, oiling, galvanizing (zinc coating) or sacrificial protection.

items.name: Groups vs periods
items.formula: group number = outer-shell electrons; period = number of shells
items.notes: Group 0: noble gases (full shells, unreactive); Group VII: halogens; Group I: alkali metals.

items.name: Trend across a period
items.formula: atomic radius decreases; electronegativity and ionization energy increase
items.notes: Stronger nuclear pull on the same shell.

items.name: Trend down a group
items.formula: reactivity increases (Group I), decreases (Group VII); melting/boiling falls (I), rises (VII)
items.notes: Extra shells shield the outer electrons.

items.name: Ionic bonding
items.formula: metal → non-metal electron TRANSFER, e.g. MgCl₂
items.notes: Giant lattice; conducts when molten/aqueous, not solid; high m.p.

items.name: Covalent bonding
items.formula: non-metal ↔ non-metal electron SHARING, e.g. CH₄
items.notes: Simple molecules: low m.p./b.p., do not conduct.

items.name: Alkanes
items.formula: general formula CnH₂n₊₂; CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀
items.notes: Saturated (single bonds); burn in O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O (fuels).

items.name: Alkenes / alcohols
items.formula: alkenes: CnH₂n (C=C double bond); alcohols: –OH group
items.notes: Test for unsaturation: bromine water decolourised (orange → colourless).

items.name: Gases: H₂ / O₂ / NH₃
items.formula: H₂: squeaky pop; O₂: relights glowing splint; NH₃: damp red litmus → blue
items.notes: CO₂: limewater milky. Cl₂: bleaches damp litmus.

items.name: Water in a sample
items.formula: blue cobalt chloride → pink; white anhydrous CuSO₄ → blue
items.notes: Both test for the presence of water.

items.name: Haber process (ammonia)
items.formula: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (iron catalyst, ~450 °C, 200 atm)
items.notes: Compromise conditions: good rate without killing the yield.

items.name: Contact process (sulfuric acid)
items.formula: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅ catalyst)
items.notes: SO₃ absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ to make oleum, then diluted.

items.name: Blast furnace
items.formula: reducing agent is carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂
items.notes: Limestone removes impurities as slag.

items.name: Aluminium extraction
items.formula: electrolysis of bauxite in molten cryolite
items.notes: Cryolite lowers the melting point, saving energy.
